decided_by: Claude (Opus) re-checking vendor docs; the human delegated this step

3:access.note: Pipedrive docs: private app 'can be shared with any company in Pipedrive via its direct, unlisted installation link' - no approval needed (pipedrive.readme.io/docs/marketplace-registering-a-private-app)

3:verdict.note: Free dev sandbox + unlisted OAuth app installable by any company

11:mcp.note: No Zendesk-owned doc for a Zendesk MCP server; Zendesk docs only cover an MCP *client* (support.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/10497779528730). The only 'official server' claim is a third-party blog. Listed servers are Swifteq/GitHub community.

22:primary_auth.note: twilio.com/docs/usage/requests-to-twilio: 'Use your API key as the username and your API key secret as the password'. Twilio Connect OAuth is legacy/niche.

22:mcp.note: twilio.com/docs/ai/mcp: 'The Twilio Model Context Protocol (MCP) server gives AI coding agents direct, structured access to Twilio's full API'

29:access.note: developer.aircall.io OAuth tutorial: 'OAuth credentials - If you haven't received them yet, apply to the Tech Partner program.'

36:verdict.note: Klaviyo OAuth docs: 'Your app does not have to be listed to share and use your installation URL' - free account, no gate

41:access.note: shopify.dev/docs/apps/launch/distribution: public distribution (needed for multiple stores) 'requires Shopify approval'

41:mcp.note: shopify.dev documents Shopify's own Dev MCP and Storefront MCP servers

54:primary_auth.note: docs.mrscraper.com calls it an 'API Token' ('API Tokens allow you to securely access the MrScraper API'); rubric: static tokens not called API key = bearer_token. Blind checker was wrong here.

59:access.note: waterfall.io only offers 'Book a Call' / 'Book a demo'; no self-serve signup or free credits found. Blind checker's 'free credits' came from unverified search snippets.

59:mcp.note: No MCP page in docs.waterfall.io/llms.txt and no server found in search

59:verdict.note: Sales-led access (book a call) before any API key

62:access.note: Any Vercel account (incl. free Hobby) can create access tokens (vercel.com/docs/rest-api/authentication); fact-checker's 'paid_plan' is wrong

62:verdict.note: Free tokens + OAuth integrations, broad REST API, official MCP

82:access.note: Free self-serve Sandbox keys (plaid.com/docs); full Production needs Plaid review, counted as friction in verdict

82:verdict.note: Production access requires an application/review by Plaid and end users must go through Plaid Link

84:access.note: No product called 'Paygent Connect' tied to NMI could be found; NMI gateway credentials are issued via a merchant account/reseller. Low confidence - Gemini's 'free self-serve' is unsupported.

84:mcp.note: No Paygent/NMI MCP server found; Gemini first pass 'official' unsupported

84:verdict.note: Product identity unclear; credentials only via merchant/reseller relationship

92:primary_auth.note: Otter's own remote MCP server (mcp.otter.ai) signs users in with OAuth - the path an integration would use

92:access.note: Otter REST API is Enterprise-only: 'contact your Otter account manager to enable access' (help.otter.ai public API article)

92:verdict.note: Official OAuth MCP usable today; full REST API needs Enterprise

99:primary_auth.note: transcriptapi.com: key sent as 'Authorization: Bearer API_KEY', vendor calls it an API key; no OAuth
